30 test rows · log loss: lower is better. Table order is descriptive;

CV choice: Neural network

?How the default model was chosen

Neural network was selected using 5-fold cross-validation on the
training rows. 15 settings were tried; one fitted representative per
successful family is kept here.[Inspect the search](#selection)Score
definitions

?Score definitions

log loss: Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers;
lower is better. Brier score: Unscaled mean sum of squared errors across
all class probabilities, from 0 (best) to 2 (worst); lower is better.
Its scale depends on the class set, so do not compare it directly with
binary Brier scores or scores for a differently defined outcome. binned
calibration gap: Average absolute gap between grouped probabilities and
observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value depends on the
evaluation sample and grouping. accuracy: Share of evaluation rows
assigned to the correct class; higher is better. macro recall: Recall
calculated for each class and then averaged equally; higher is better.
Unavailable when any trained class is absent from the evaluation rows.

How costs were measured

Times are measured on this machine. Fit time covers the retained fit,
not the entire cross-validation search; prediction time covers this
evaluation batch. A displayed ~0 means no elapsed time was recorded;
timer resolution varies by platform. It does not mean the operation
takes no time. Size is an approximate R object measurement, not a count
of learned rules. These measurements are not hardware-independent
benchmarks.

Measure repeated prediction costs

A single timer reading can be too coarse for small models. Measure
repeated predictions on a common batch to compare their costs.

```
bench <- benchmark_predictions(result)
render_model_report(result, "report.html", benchmark = bench)
```

## Why these settings?

Training-only cross-validation; lower loss is better. These CV scores
are not final performance estimates.

Lowest CV loss

Policy choice

Final primary fit

**0.054 log loss**Neural network · 2 units; decay 0.03 (same
configuration)

Neural network was the first preferred family within the allowed loss of
0.0619. Its chosen setting had the smallest recorded capacity proxy
among eligible settings in that family; score breaks a proxy tie.

No complete resampling result: Multinomial logistic (linear). These
families have no retained fit from the corresponding stage.

### Neural network: search rationale

Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the
search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized
using each training fold. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5
untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

**Tested:** size: 2, 6, 4, 8, 1 · decay: 0.03, 0.01, 0.001, 0.1

The family CV winner is interior on every varied numeric control in the
scheduled range.

allowed loss. Fold scores show variability, not confidence intervals.
Each family has its own numeric scale.

### Decision tree: search rationale

Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward
deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row
count, bounded below by four. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5
untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

**Tested:** maxdepth: 6, 5, 10, 8, 4, 2, 3 · cp: 0.003, 0.0005, 0.001,
0.01, 0.03 · minsplit: 10, 6, 14, 24

Exact selection arithmetic and preference order

Eligible loss ≤ 0.040841 + 0.021087 = **0.061928**. Among eligible
candidates: first the preferred family, then its smallest recorded
capacity proxy, then score and configuration ID to break a tie.

| Family               | Preference order | Within-family capacity proxy       |
|----------------------|------------------|------------------------------------|
| Multinomial logistic | 1                | potential coefficient count        |
| Decision tree        | 4                | within-family potential leaf count |
| Neural network       | 9                | within-family connection count     |

Values: Family, Preference order, Within-family capacity proxy

Family order is package or user preference. Capacity proxies omit some
regularization controls; they do not establish a universal
least-flexible model.

CV loss is averaged across validation rows, weighting folds by their
evaluated row counts. Fold-score SE is a selection heuristic. Training
folds overlap; it is not a confidence interval, equivalence test or
population uncertainty.

Preprocessing was learned again inside every fold. The evaluation
partition was not used to choose hyperparameters. Full fold assignments
and any retained out-of-fold predictions remain in
`tuning_results(result)`.

Why this grid? Coverage, parameter meaning and boundary winners

Round-robin ordered grid prefixes; explicit family budgets override the
total allocation. Outer training rows: 120; raw inputs: 4.

Exact preset numbers are package engineering choices, not values
justified as optimal by literature. This finite joint-configuration
search does not identify causal effects of individual settings.

| Family | Grid source | Available tuples | Scheduled tuples | Untested tuples | Rationale |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| linear | package_presets | 1 | 1 | 0 | One unpenalized reference fit; there is no parameter grid for this family. |
| tree | package_presets | 12 | 7 | 5 | Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row count, bounded below by four. |
| neural | package_presets | 12 | 7 | 5 | Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized using each training fold. |

Recorded search budget and rationale

| Family | Parameter | Available preset values | Meaning |
|----|----|----|----|
| tree | maxdepth | 2, 4, 6, 10, 3, 5, 8 | Maximum permitted tree depth, not observed depth. |
| tree | cp | 0.03, 0.01, 0.003, 0.0005, 0.001, 0 | Larger thresholds discourage small-improvement splits. |
| tree | minsplit | 24, 14, 10, 6, 4 | Minimum training rows in a node before attempting a split. |
| neural | size | 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 | Hidden units in one layer; more units permit more patterns. |
| neural | decay | 0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001, 0, 0.0001 | Weight penalty; larger values discourage large weights. |

Available values and parameter meanings

| family | configuration_id | parameter | selected_value | tested_min | tested_max | distinct_values | position |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| neural | neural_04 | size | 6.00 | 1.00 | 8.00 | 5 | interior |
| neural | neural_04 | decay | 0.01 | 0.001 | 0.10 | 4 | interior |
| tree | tree_03 | maxdepth | 6.00 | 2.00 | 10.00 | 7 | interior |
| tree | tree_03 | cp | 0.003 | 5e-04 | 0.03 | 5 | interior |
| tree | tree_03 | minsplit | 10.00 | 6.00 | 24.00 | 4 | interior |

Position of each family CV winner within scheduled numeric settings

A fixed setting was not varied. An edge winner can motivate a new
training-only comparison; it does not show that extending one control
would help, because several controls may differ between the tested
tuples.

Refit attempts; evaluation scores do not choose a fallback

Copy and change this search grid in R

This executable control reproduces the scheduled tuples and budgets.
Edit a tuple to test a specific hypothesis. Refit using your original
data, preprocessing, validation design and seed. This control alone does
not reproduce the entire analysis. Avoid repeatedly tuning against the
evaluation partition.

    control <- tuning_control(
      grids = list(linear = list(list()), tree = list(list(maxdepth = 2L, cp = 0.03,
        minsplit = 24L), list(maxdepth = 4L, cp = 0.01, minsplit = 14L),
        list(maxdepth = 6L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 10L), list(maxdepth = 10L,
            cp = 5e-04, minsplit = 6L), list(maxdepth = 3L, cp = 0.01,
            minsplit = 24L), list(maxdepth = 5L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 10L),
        list(maxdepth = 8L, cp = 0.001, minsplit = 6L)), neural = list(
        list(size = 1L, decay = 0.1), list(size = 2L, decay = 0.03),
        list(size = 4L, decay = 0.01), list(size = 6L, decay = 0.01),
        list(size = 8L, decay = 0.001), list(size = 2L, decay = 0.001),
        list(size = 4L, decay = 0.001))),
      family_budgets = c(linear = 1L, tree = 7L, neural = 7L),
      metric = "log_loss",
      optimization_policy = "exclude",
      family_priority = c("linear", "tree", "neural")
    )
    # In your original autoxplain(...) call, use:
    #   learners = c("linear", "tree", "neural"), max_models = NULL, tuning_control = control
    #   tuning_rule = "one_se", seed = 33
    # Keep the original preprocessing and validation design (including supplied fold IDs).

Use `tuning_evidence(result)` for the aggregate record.

Method references and limits

These sources explain selection bias, fold variability and backend
controls. They do not validate this package’s exact preset numbers or
family preference order.

- [Selection bias and holdout
  separation](https://jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
- [Fold variability](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v5/grandvalet04a.html)
- [Search design
  baseline](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v13/bergstra12a.html)
- [Regularization and lambda
  paths](https://glmnet.stanford.edu/articles/glmnet.html)
- [Neural
  optimization](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/nnet/html/nnet.html)
- [Tree
  controls](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/rpart/html/rpart.control.html)

Checks

## What needs a closer look?

Findings identify their affected model or input. [Data
distributions](#data) and [prediction diagnostics](#evaluation) have
their own views.

### Important context for these scores

### Only 30 rows were available for test scoring.

**Next step:** Treat the scores as preliminary and validate on more
representative rows.

### Every attempted configuration failed in at least one training-only fold for: linear.

**Next step:** Inspect \`tuning_results(result)\$fold_scores\$error\`;
these families were excluded from selection and cannot be compared using
complete out-of-fold evidence.

## Checks requiring attention

No diagnostic findings were recorded. Review the coverage below; an
absent finding is not a guarantee.

Diagnostic coverage and association evidence

**evaluation: computed.** Ordered observations, outcomes and event
semantics agree; independence and representativeness are not established
by these checks.

**association: computed.** Limited pairwise screen: absolute Spearman
correlation for numeric pairs, correlation ratio for mixed pairs, and
Cramer's V for categorical pairs. Small values do not establish
independence or exclude nonlinear or joint dependence.

**permutation: computed.** Loss changes describe these shuffles. The
intervals quantify shuffle randomness, not sampling, fitting or
selection uncertainty.

**comparison: insufficient evidence.** Fewer than two supplied models
meet the performance tolerance.

**resources: computed.**

**model_behavior: computed.**

**prediction_disagreement: computed.**

**decision_cutoffs: not applicable.** Decision-cutoff comparisons apply
to binary classification.

| model | features | no_observed_change | positive_loss_change | negative_loss_change | interval_includes_zero | interval_unavailable |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| main_model | 4 | 0 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| tree_model | 4 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| simple_baseline | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Checks by supplied model

Separate descriptive diagnostics; no overall evidence grade. Shuffle
intervals omit evaluation-sampling, fitting and selection uncertainty.

## How variable is this score?

Paired 95.0% percentile intervals from 1000 bootstrap draws over 30
observations. Negative differences favor the primary model.

| quantity   | estimate | lower  | upper  |
|------------|----------|--------|--------|
| primary    | 0.166    | 0.021  | 0.39   |
| baseline   | 1.099    | 1.099  | 1.099  |
| difference | -0.932   | -1.078 | -0.708 |

Values: quantity, estimate, lower

Paired percentile intervals conditional on the fitted models; negative
differences favor the primary model. These intervals omit fitting and
selection uncertainty and assume independent sampling units.

No missing input values were observed in training or evaluation.

information. Filtering or hiding a panel does not remove embedded
content.

Metric definitions

Definitions for every metric

- log loss: Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers;
  lower is better.
- Brier score: Unscaled mean sum of squared errors across all class
  probabilities, from 0 (best) to 2 (worst); lower is better. Its scale
  depends on the class set, so do not compare it directly with binary
  Brier scores or scores for a differently defined outcome.
- binned calibration gap: Average absolute gap between grouped
  probabilities and observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value
  depends on the evaluation sample and grouping.
- accuracy: Share of evaluation rows assigned to the correct class;
  higher is better.
- macro recall: Recall calculated for each class and then averaged
  equally; higher is better. Unavailable when any trained class is
  absent from the evaluation rows.

### Reading this analysis

Scores describe the recorded evaluation split. Feature effects describe
fitted associations. Use independent evaluation data for a final
assessment after changing models or predictors. Neither this report nor
a passing diagnostic establishes causal effects.
